Decisions should involve the patient and family, reflect the available evidence, and remain specific to the individual. brain.title: Brain & neurological conditions
brain.summary: Neurosurgical evaluation for selected conditions affecting the brain and nervous system.
brain.body: Neurosurgery is one part of a wider care team. Some neurological symptoms require surgical assessment; many are investigated and managed by neurologists, physicians, or other specialists. A consultation is a chance to clarify what is happening, review the available imaging and tests, and decide which kind of care is appropriate.
scope: Coordination with neurology and other specialties
brain.link: What to expect at a consultation

neurotrauma.title: Complex neurotrauma
neurotrauma.summary: Assessment and care of significant injury involving the brain, spine, or nervous system.
neurotrauma.body: Neurotrauma covers a wide range of injury, from a minor blow to the head to a serious injury involving the brain or spinal cord. The response should match the severity. A routine clinic appointment is not appropriate for an acute emergency. Confusion, repeated vomiting, seizures, weakness, or loss of consciousness after a head injury need urgent assessment.

spine.title: Spine & spinal interventions
spine.summary: Neurosurgical assessment of selected spinal conditions affecting nerves or the spinal cord.
spine.body: Many spinal symptoms improve with time and non-surgical care. Neurosurgical input is usually considered when there is a specific pattern of nerve compression, instability, or another finding that may benefit from intervention. Imaging is interpreted together with the history and examination, not in isolation.
scope: Review of prior imaging and reports

research.title: Brain disorder research
research.summary: A professional interest in the causes, patterns, and care of neurological disease.
research.body: Research helps clinical practice ask better questions. Dr. Zadran's stated interest includes brain disorder research and neurotrauma. The public record currently lists one verified journal publication; research interests are not presented as completed projects, unpublished findings, or a broader publication record.

technology.title: Surgical technology
technology.summary: The responsible use of modern tools within neurological care.
technology.body: Modern neurosurgery draws on imaging, navigation, monitoring, and other technologies where they are appropriate and available. Technology can improve precision and safety, but it supports clinical judgement rather than replacing it. No specific equipment, navigation system, or robotic capability is attributed to the doctor or clinic on this website without confirmation.

consultation.heading: A conversation, an examination, a plan.
consultation.intro: A consultation is not a single fixed script. What happens depends on the concern and the information available. It may include the following elements.

steps.title: History
steps.body: A discussion of symptoms, their timing, relevant medical history, and the impact on daily life.

steps.title: Examination
steps.body: A focused physical and neurological examination where appropriate.

steps.title: Review
steps.body: Review of imaging, reports, medications, and tests brought to the consultation.

steps.title: Discussion
steps.body: An explanation of what is known, what remains uncertain, and which options may be relevant.

steps.title: Next steps
steps.body: Further tests, a non-surgical plan, a surgical discussion, or referral may be considered. No outcome is guaranteed.

consultation.note: This describes a typical process in general terms. It is not a promise of what will happen at a particular appointment.

emergency.heading: Some symptoms should not wait.
emergency.body: A serious head or spinal injury, a seizure, or a sudden neurological change can require emergency medical assessment. Do not use this website, social media, or a routine clinic call as an emergency response service.
signs: Sudden weakness or numbness, especially on one side
A seizure, especially a first seizure
Loss of consciousness or worsening confusion
Repeated vomiting or severe headache after a head injury
A serious injury to the head, neck, or spine

emergency.note: If you are unsure how serious a symptom is, seek urgent medical advice rather than waiting.

method.heading: How a record is verified.
method.body: Records are checked against PubMed and DOI metadata. Author affiliation, subject matter, and the doctor's public professional identity are considered together. A matching name alone is not treated as proof of identity. Items that cannot be attributed with reasonable confidence are omitted rather than guessed.

publications.emptyBody: This page is ready for publication records, but none can be attributed with sufficient confidence at present. No placeholder research has been added. Verified records will appear here when available.

tawhid2025.summary: An observational case-control study at Ali Abad University Hospital in Kabul, comparing 64 patients with brain tumors and 159 matched controls. The authors reported an association between a history of head injury and a brain tumor diagnosis. The study design can show an association, not causation.
tawhid2025.note: The publication reports an association. It does not establish that head injury causes brain tumors.
